claims: Released 1999; largest Rock Raiders set; 402 pieces for four minifigures, a Rock Monster, a base and two vehicles.
The HQ has an energy production/storage area, a boulder splitter, a place which drops boulders onto vehicles, a laser for drilling or fighting Rock Monsters, and a crane.
The crane lowers, raises and carries boulders; the laser is on the tallest part of the base and rotates.
The crystal is placed in the energy production/storage area; the boulder-splitting area holds a boulder whose top is taken off by the crane.
The base is mostly bright bluish green, bright yellow and grey.
Vehicles: a small four-wheeler with a boulder bucket (yellow, teal, dark grey) and a small hovercraft piloted by Jet.

The structure is composed of four major buildings resembling the video game's Upgrade Station (the Crane), Mining Laser (the Brickonium Blaster), Teleport Pad (parking space for the hovercraft) and the top of the Power Station (used to cut open rocks), plus a building that carries and deposits LEGO ore boulders.
The Brickonium Blaster needs two AAA batteries; the set includes a light brick.
Minifigures: Bandit, Docs, Jet, Sparks; plus a Rock Monster.
The Teleport Pad appears in 4990, where it serves as a parking space for a small hovercraft.

The four main sections could be swapped around in any order and interacted: the crane lifts a rock to the small laser, the rock is cut open and the crystal removed, then the crane moves it to the dumper, which tips it into the truck.
sources.note: Fan commentary; used only as corroboration of the modular, swappable section design.

textCorroborated: 4990 is a modular playset: four swappable sections on one raised baseplate, plus two vehicles, four minifigures and a Rock Monster.

Sections: a crane (lifts and carries boulders), a rotating light-up Mining Laser on the tallest part, a Teleport Pad used as the hovercraft parking/dock, a Power Station top with the crystal energy store and a boulder splitter (small laser), and a boulder dumper that drops boulders onto a vehicle.
The base is the light-grey raised baseplate 30271px3 (32 x 48 studs) with four corner pits and a printed rock pattern.

The base palette is dominated by bright bluish green (LEGO's name for dark turquoise), bright yellow and grey; the Faction Bible independently records dark turquoise and dark grey as the Rock Raiders primaries.
The rotating laser is the dark-grey 30346c01 light assembly (4 x 12 x 2 studs), shared only with 4970 Chrome Crusher.
adaptedInTarget: Square 40 x 40-stud plinth (8 x 8 cells, 16 x 16 m) replacing the 32 x 48 baseplate; area 1600 vs 1536 studs squared keeps module sizes relative to the minifigure at 1 stud = 0.4 m.
Section arrangement for the game footprint and camera (tall section at the north-west back corner).
Mining Laser presented as a non-firing rotating work beam.
Teleport Pad presented as the Crew production pad with a south ramp to the 2 x 2 production exit.
Boulder dumper presented as the emergency Ore receiving bay.
Two flat team Identification Tiles; restrained lane hazard decal.
unknownOrDisputed: Exact construction, height and colour distribution of every section, including what carries the laser on the tallest part.
Exact relief, pit shape and section seating on 30271px3, and how the four sections sit on it.
Lens colour of the light assembly.
Whether a conveyor exists: the T082 page map mentions a conveyor/processing module; no text source mentions one. The T085 target does not add a conveyor.
Whether the crane is mounted on the tower (T082 wording) or is a separate section (text sources call it a separate building). The T085 target treats it as a separate section.
correctionsToEarlierT082Draft: T082 names a power tower, a crane mounted to it, a vehicle gantry and a conveyor. Independent text sources name a rotating light-up Mining Laser on the tallest part, a separate crane section, a Teleport Pad, a Power Station top and a boulder dumper. The gantry wording is compatible with the dumper over a vehicle lane; the conveyor is uncorroborated. The T082 packet is preserved unchanged; the official pages must settle the difference.
